name: Beaverfolk
body:
Beaverfolk are rodentlike humanoids common to rivers, lakes, and wetlands.

Appearance

Only slightly larger than actual beavers, beaverfolk look very much like the animals they are named after, although their bodies are more streamlined and humanoid in shape. They usually have brown or gray fur and black eyes, although there are exceptions. They have slightly webbed hands and feet and broad, flat tails that both help them swim and help maintain their stability. They have four powerful, chisel-shaped incisors that continue to grow throughout their lives, allowing them to bite with considerable force.

Social

Beaverfolk are known for being extremely hardworking and industrious, almost to a fault. They sometimes have difficulty stopping work in order to engage in diversions or social discourse.

Beaverfolk are devoted to their families, often showing them the same kind of obsessiveness that they show their occupations. Compulsive grooming and a preoccupation with tidiness is not uncommon.

Beaverfolk have a great respect for nature, but they also firmly believe that natural forces are meant to be bent to their will. As consummate engineers, they are constantly evaluating new plans for dams, ditches, trenches, channels, and earth-moving projects great and small. Traditionally, they build their homes atop the water out of logs and mud-entire beaverfolk cities rising up in seemingly haphazard fashion to connect the swamp.

Alignment and Religion

One would think that beaverfolk would have a strong predilection toward Lawful alignments due to their compulsive need to focus on their work. However, the split between Law, Chaos, and Neutrality is more or less even among them-some devoted to upholding traditional building styles, while others see themselves as artistic souls with a need to follow their own visions, and still others having the practicality to adapt their build to the situation.

Most beaverfolk lean toward Good or Neutrality, but as they are reserved in their affections some do lose sight of basic decency and develop Evil tendencies.

While they are customarily very reserved in their expressions of faith, most beaverfolk do practice some form of religion. Many of them worship nature or a nature god of some kind, but some worship deities devoted to protection, community, engineering, craftsmanship, or industry. To worship a god devoted to leisure is considered heresy of the highest order.

Names

Some typical beaverfolk names include the following (choose or roll 1d12): 1 Bûcheron, 2 Charmant, 3 Constructeur, 4 Coupeur, 5 Coureur, 6 Industrieux, 7 Ingénieur, 8 Menuisier, 9 Nageur, 10 Robuste, 11 Travailleur, 12 Voyageur

Common Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are hardy and industrious but short on charm. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Con, +2 Int, -2 Cha [standard]. (0)
Size As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type You are a Humanoid with the beaverfolk subtype. (0)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Sylvan. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Aquan, Draconic, Elven, Gnome, Goblin, and Halfling. (0)
Other Traits
Hold Breath You can hold your breath for a number of rounds equal to four times your Constitution score before risking drowning or suffocating. (1)
Low-light vision You can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. You retain the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions. (1)
Obsessive You receive a +2 species bonus on a Craft or Profession skill of your choice. (2)
Stability You use your wide tail to steady yourself. You gain a +4 species bonus to your CMD when resisting a bull rush or trip attempt while standing on the ground. (1)
Sundering Bite You gain a bite attack. This is a primary natural weapon that deals 1d4 damage for a Medium beaverfolk (1d3 if Small). Additionally, your bite ignores the first 5 points of an object’s hardness. (3)
Swim You have a swim speed of 30 feet and gain the +8 species bonus on Swim checks that a swim speed normally grants. (2)
Total: 10 RP (standard)
Alternate Traits
Balanced You know how to use your tail to maintain your balance and gain the advantage in a tight spot. Acrobatics and Escape Artist are always class skills for you. This trait replaces hold breath.
Barricade Your experience building dams also comes in handy in other situations. You gain Barricade* as a bonus feat. You do not need to meet this feat’s usual prerequisites. This trait replaces obsessive.
Climb You’re more accustomed to climbing on branches than swimming in rivers. You have a climb speed of 20 feet, and gain the +8 species bonus on Climb checks that a climb speed normally grants. This trait replaces swim.
Intuitive Some beaverfolk rely more on their experience and gut instinct than on carefully-made plans. You gain a +2 bonus to Wisdom instead of a bonus to Intelligence. This trait alters ability score bonuses.
Keen Senses Some beaverfolk serve as lookouts for their communities, obsessing about their roles as sentries rather than as artisans. You gain a +2 species bonus to Perception checks. This trait replaces obsessive.
Slapping Tail Some beaverfolk use their tails to protect themselves rather than to stabilize themselves. You gain a tail slap attack. This is a secondary natural attack that deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage for a Medium beaverfolk (1d4 if Small). This trait replaces stability.
Small You’re slighter of build than most beaverfolk. You are size Small. This trait alters size.
Swamp Stride You can move through difficult terrain at your normal speed while within a swamp or other wetland terrain. Magically altered terrain affects you normally. This trait replaces obsessive.
Weapon Familiarity You are proficient with the battleaxe, greataxe, handaxe, and mattock UC. You treat the dwarven waraxe and dwarven double waraxe ARG as martial weapons instead of exotic ones. This trait replaces sundering bite.
Favored Class Bonuses
Alchemist Gain +1/6 of a new discovery.
Barbarian While you are raging, the hardness ignored by your sundering bite increases by +1/2 point.
Cleric Select one domain power granted at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Wisdom modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that domain power.
Druid Add +1 hit point to your animal companion. If you ever replace your animal companion, the new animal companion gains these bonus hit points.
Fighter Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a bull rush or trip attempt.
Gunslinger Add +1/4 to the number of grit points in your grit pool.
Monk Add a +1/4 bonus on combat maneuver checks made to grapple or sunder.
Ranger Add +1 hit point to your animal companion. If you ever replace your animal companion, the new animal companion gains these bonus hit points.
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on Disable Device checks regarding traps made primarily of wood, ropes, leather, and other organic materials, and a +1/2 bonus to trap sense regarding traps made primarily of wood and other organic materials.
Scholar Add +1/4 to your effective scholar level and number of ranks in Knowledge (engineering) for the purpose of determining the effects of all basic and advanced study abilities associated with the engineering study.
Shaman Add +1 spell from the druid spell list that isn’t on the shaman spell list to the list of spells you can prepare as a shaman. This spell must be at least one spell level lower than the highest-level shaman spell you can cast.
Sorcerer Choose a terrain type from the ranger‘s favored terrain list. When casting sorcerer spells in the chosen terrain, add +1/3 to the effective caster level of the spell, for the purpose of determining the spell’s duration.
Spirit Warrior Add +1 to the total number of rounds per day that you can use your aura ability.
Witch Add a +1/2 bonus on concentration checks to cast witch spells. This bonus doubles in a swamp or water terrain.
Wizard Select one arcane school power at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Intelligence modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that arcane school power.
